Global Pioneers Family Visitor Morning Sat 10 October
Saturday 10 October, 9.00am for prospective families with children looking to join Reception 2027/28
Booking is essential as places are strictly limited
Join us with your children for an exciting morning of exploration with our Head of Global, Emma Austin, and Deputy Head (Innovation & Partnerships), Lex Lang.
Right from Reception, we help our pupils to develop a secure understanding of their place in an ever changing world and we do this through our bespoke Global and EDGE curriculums.
This dedicated morning for prospective families invites you to visit our Pre-Prep School to meet our team while your child gets stuck into some fun filled discoveries.
Children will get hands on as they travel the globe with some exciting and innovative activities.
Parents will have the opportunity to talk to our staff over refreshments.
Places for this event are limited so please book early. This event is most suitable for 2-4 year olds.
BOOK YOUR TICKETS

CATERHAM PREP
Headmaster’s Welcome
Wellbeing

Drama
Drama is central to pupils learning at Caterham Prep, through Drama pupils reinforce topic work, they develop their speaking and listening skills and they strengthen literacy.
Pupils from Reception to Year 6 have a Drama lesson each week. Drama lessons take place in the many great performance spaces across the school including the purpose built prep drama studio. Pupils explore stories, characters and develop the skills needed to shape, create and perform. As pupils progress through the school, they explore a range of play texts including Shakespeare, they learn about a range of Drama genres/styles, and they delve into the history of theatre. Drama strives to build pupils’ confidence, communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively with others. Through commitment and curiosity pupils will learn new ways to present and perform, building valuable life skills for the future.
Here at Caterham Prep we run a successful and fun filled LAMDA program. Pupils in Years 3-6 are given the opportunity to sign up for LAMDA clubs during a lunchtime or after school slot. Pupils explore a wide range of disciplines in LAMDA lessons from Speaking of Verse and Prose, Drama for Performance, Solo and Duologue Acting and Presenting. Pupils can take exams in all these disciplines and most pupils take 2-3 exams a year. LAMDA builds confidence and independence on stage. It teaches pupils to present themselves well and communicate effectively with an audience.
We run a rich co-curricular programme in Drama with pupils getting the opportunity to take part in fun lunchtime or after school clubs. Dance clubs are offered by our specialist Performing Arts assistant and are very popular. Drama club pupils also prepare an annual pantomime performed for the rest of the school.
Drama is an essential part of the curriculum at Caterham Prep. Each year group gets to perform their own production on stage each year. This year group show is a time for all the children to come together, for pupils to build their collaboration skills and understand the important of commitment and confidence on stage. Productions take place in our beautiful Soderberg Hall and Year 6 get to perform on the big stage in the impressive 330 seat Humphreys Theatre. Recent productions have included Matilda, Shrek and The Lion King. We are currently working on productions of Oliver, Fantastic Mr Fox and we are excited to start Year 5’s Shakespearean piece which will be based on The Tempest. Pupils are also invited to perform on the outdoor stage at the senior school Orchard Theatre Festival in the Summer Term.

Busy Bees Toddler Group
WEEKLY Busy Bees Toddler Group
Every Thursday 9.30am to 10.30am based in our Outdoor Classroom at Pre-Prep.
Weekly child led woodland play group designed for families of preschool children considering joining Caterham Prep. Based in our outdoor classroom, nestled within our own woodland, there is something to spark curiosity in every young adventurer. Activities will be led by our Head of Outdoor Learning, Mrs Lauren du Plooy and may involve some time in our yurt. Each session will conclude with group story time, perfect for winding down after all the excitement. Keep an eye out for special weeks when we will venture out on a woodland walk, there is so much to see!
There is no charge to join the group although we kindly ask you to reserve your place in advance to ensure that we can accommodate everyone. We will provide refreshments (including hot chocolate when the weather is a bit chilly!) for children and parents/guardians. Sessions will take place in all weathers because a little rain never spoils our fun! In the case of lightning storms or high winds, we will advise alternative plans. Please dress appropriately for the weather and we advise to bring a change of clothes and shoes. To book a space on a weekly session, please click on the booking links below.

Headmaster’s Welcome
Wellbeing

Art
At Caterham Prep, children from Year 2 to Year 6 enjoy weekly Art lessons in our dedicated Art room, led by a specialist Art teacher. These lessons give pupils the opportunity to develop their imagination, creativity, observational skills, analytical and problem–solving skills whilst also continually gaining a deeper knowledge and understanding of a range of media, processes, art and artists. They explore a wide variety of themes, often linked to their Global topics, giving them the chance to make connections across subjects. Children experiment with a range of media, including painting, printmaking, textiles, and digital art. Additionally, each year group has the opportunity to work on a ceramics project, glazing and firing their own work in our kiln.
Beyond the curriculum, we offer co-curricular creative clubs- a weekly Art club aimed at Year 3 and 4 pupils, and another dedicated to Year 5 and 6 pupils. For those interested in developing their artistic skills further, we also run an after-school stretch and challenge Portfolio Club aimed at pupils considering applying for an 11+ Art scholarship.
Our pupils participate in local and national Art competitions ranging from the East Surrey MP’s Christmas Card competition to the Royal Academy of Arts Young Artists Summer Show. In addition, some of their artwork has also been displayed in our local community. Our goal for art education is to promote enjoyment, creativity and developing skills which will last a lifetime.

English
Our pupils are taught to read, but also read to learn.
At Caterham Prep, English is more than a subject—it’s a gateway to developing essential skills for life. Through a rich curriculum that integrates reading, writing, and oracy, pupils explore high-quality texts linked to their Global topic, allowing them to engage with ideas that shape the world around them.
Reading is an essential part of a pupils’ Caterham Prep journey, and it is our aim to foster a love of this throughout. Pupils experience a range of initiatives from mystery readers to author visits and dedicated reading areas across the School. Pupils are also encouraged to engage with our carefully curated reading lists, which contain texts suited to all abilities, different genres, as well as linking to their Global topics to further facilitate knowledge and understanding.
We believe that language is a tool for thinking and creating. Through our texts and thought-provoking questions, our English lessons encourage talk, debate and deep thinking. Pupils analyse, reflect and imitate outstanding writing, learning to apply sentence structures, imaginative devices and vocabulary to a variety of different writing outcomes, preparing them for life beyond school.

Maths
At Caterham Prep, we believe that maths is not just about numbers and calculations; it’s about developing problem-solving skills, creativity, and the confidence to tackle challenges. It is not solely a subject taught at school, but in fact a life skill. Our approach to teaching maths is all about making learning fun, engaging, and relevant to every child. By making lessons interactive, hands-on, and enjoyable, we help children see the exciting possibilities that maths offers. Whether it’s solving puzzles, playing games, or using real-world examples, we believe that a positive attitude towards maths can set the foundation for success and lifelong enjoyment of the subject.
We understand that every child learns differently. Some may excel at mental arithmetic, while others might find patterns and puzzles more engaging. That’s why we tailor our lessons to suit different learning styles and abilities. We encourage every child to explore maths at their own pace, ensuring that they are both challenged and supported throughout their learning journey. We have a strong belief in building independent learners and help to develop their understanding and awareness of what they personally need to progress and what they need to do to get there.
One of the key principles we promote in our maths classes is a growth mindset—the belief that with effort and perseverance, anyone can improve their abilities. Instead of focusing on mistakes as failures, we view them as opportunities for growth and learning. We celebrate progress, big or small, and encourage our children to tackle maths problems with confidence, knowing that they can always improve.
By fostering a love for maths early on, we lay the foundation for our children’s future academic success. From developing logical reasoning to enhancing critical thinking skills, our engaging, collaborative and enjoyable approach to maths prepares our children for the challenges of secondary school and beyond.

Wellbeing
Timetabled wellbeing lessons are a cornerstone of our school wide approach to wellbeing from Reception right through to Upper Sixth Form in the senior school.
Age-appropriate lessons empower our pupils to thrive personally and socially, to form positive relationships and to embrace inclusivity and diversity. Year group and class assemblies complement lessons, presenting key topics including mental health and promoting deeper exploration in class. Through these platforms pupils become equipped with the tools, knowledge and understanding to make informed decisions about their own health and wellbeing. Through increasing their self-awareness, they will develop a sense of identity and learn how to contribute positively to society. The curriculum aims to foster confidence and resilience, enabling pupils to achieve and persevere through challenges, building strong foundations for life.

Headmaster’s Welcome
Inspiring education for life
Caterham Prep School is a vibrant and thriving part of the Caterham family, providing an outstanding education that enables every pupil to achieve his or her maximum potential intellectually, physically and creatively in an ambitious but nurturing environment.
The Caterham School community shares a 200 acre campus in the beautiful Harestone Valley and educates pupils from age 4 to 18. The Prep School is nestled at the far end of the campus, surrounded by its own woodland.
Learning how to learn is a key part of a Caterham education, from the Early Years at the Prep School to the Sixth Form at the Senior School and is, in our view, an essential skill for modern life. We believe that a truly excellent school is about more than academic achievement alone: it is also about developing a passion for learning, a capacity for problem-solving, independent and critical thinking, self-awareness and resilience, self-confidence without arrogance and genuine interests that extend beyond the confines of the classroom.
We believe in providing an ‘Education for Life’ for all Caterhamians and our innovative curriculum blends the best of tradition with exciting opportunities such as Performing Arts, Mandarin, Digital Innovation, 21st Century Skills and Global Citizenship. Our unique Outdoor Learning programme, developed in and taking advantage of our own responsibly managed forest, runs alongside all of this, together with an award-winning Wellbeing programme that runs through the heart of everything we do.
Please accept my warmest invitation to contact us for further information or to arrange a visit.
Ben Purkiss Headmaster

Pupils’ knowledge, understanding and application of technological skills are a significant strength of the school. This is the result of decisions made by leaders to focus on and resource this area. The quality of pupils’ digital work is extremely high. The highly effective and adaptive use of technology is woven throughout the entire curriculum. Technological skills, including coding and the use of artificial intelligence, are taught through the technology curriculum, which provides pupils with skills for life beyond school that are applied across all areas of learning and prepare them for life beyond school read more…
Leaders consider pupils’ welfare carefully. A pastoral structure is in place to nurture pupils. There are supportive relationships between pupils and teachers. Pupils’ wellbeing is actively promoted through the taught curriculum as well as through form time and assemblies when pupils are encourage to reflects on issues affecting their lives. Pupils develop the skills they need to navigate the transition to senior school successfully and to be confident in themselves through the many opportunities they have to take on responsibilities and to participate in school life read more…
Pupils are respectful and treat each other well. They understand who to talk to if problems arise. They show a clear moral understanding of right and wrong. Pupils are encouraged by leaders to become ‘courageous reporters’ and as a result they learn to look after themselves and each other well read more…

Leaders actively encourage a culture of inclusion and pupils show respect for different groups of people in the school and beyond. Pupils care about their school and the people in it. Older pupils value the opportunities they have to serve the school community as monitors and they take this responsibility seriously. The Journey to starting school
Before starting the admissions process, we highly recommend you join us at one of our visitor events to talk to our team, see our school and learn about life here at Caterham Prep. Our current visitor events can be found here.
You are also welcome to book a Private Tour via our Assistant Registrar (Day), Sara Chesterman who can be contacted as below:
Sara Chesterman, Assistant Registrar (Day)
Telephone: 01883 335 058
Email: [email protected].
Joining a school, particularly if it is your child’s first school, can sometimes feel a little daunting. We hope this step by step summary helps to explain what happens at each stage of the journey. Sara is always available and happy to answer any questions that you may have along the way.
Our main point of entry is Reception with two classes. Entry into all other year groups is dependent upon spaces becoming available and in this case, please contact the admissions team directly.
application
The first step is to fill out our application form which can be found here. The application and payment is confirmed to you by email along with a notification that your child has joined the relevant assessment list.
assessment
Children join Reception from their fourth birthday, which should fall on or before 31 August in their year of entry. All children applying to join our Reception class are invited to attend an assessment morning. These informal play sessions take place on a week day in the year prior to the September they would begin at school. During the session your child will complete some activities with our teachers in one of the classrooms for about 45 minutes. We ask that parents leave their child/children with us for that short time.
Children joining us higher up the school (when places become available) are invited to attend a weekday assessment afternoon. During their afternoon with us, the children will take literacy and numeracy assessments along with a fun practical session in our Innovation Centre. Dependent upon the age of your child, they may also take verbal and non verbal reasoning tests.
For all assessment sessions, we ask that parents leave their child/children with us for the entirety of the session and rest assured that with all assessment mornings/afternoons, we strive to make children feel comfortable and the experience an enjoyable one.
offer
An offer of a place can only be made once all the parent and Nursery setting questionnaires have been received for places in Reception or school references for places in other years
We offer places to pupils who will thrive with the challenging pace of learning at our school. Our decisions are truly holistic: we seek to understand your child, their strengths and interests, and the wider picture of their application including their age for their year, and any special educational needs.
We regret that we cannot offer to every applicant, though in some circumstances we invite you to remain on our waiting list.
Acceptance
An offer letter, along with an acceptance form, is sent out by email. Following receipt of the deposit along with the completed acceptance form, the place is confirmed to you by email.
Once a place has been accepted, you will be invited to a number of welcome events where you will be able to find out more about starting school along with meeting other new and existing Caterham families.
Joining forms and all information relating to starting school in September is sent midway through the Summer Term.
first day of school
Children starting School in September will be invited to visit the School in the Summer Term, prior to joining. They will have the opportunity to see their new classroom, meet their class teacher and get to know their peers.
On the first day of school, your child will be met from the car by members of our teaching team. Pupils joining us in Reception will have a slightly later start time on the first couple of days and parents will have the opportunity to bring their child up to the classroom on the first day.
Children joining further up the school will be met from the car by members of our teaching team. The form tutor will ensure that your child is introduced to the school site, where to hang coats and bags, find classrooms, go to lunch, access changing rooms for sports and introductions to friendship groups.

pageCache.pageTitle: It's All Fun and Games... and Maths! - Caterham Prep
pageCache.text:
It’s All Fun and Games… and Maths!
Year 6 have been busy putting their creativity (and maths skills!) to the test by designing and making their own maths board games. The results were incredibly impressive, with so many imaginative ideas and eye-catching designs. Lots of the games were even made in 3D, with moving pieces, pop-up features and interactive elements that brought them to life.
This week, our Year 5 pupils had the chance to try out the games, and they had a fantastic time solving the maths challenges, playing against their friends and voting for their favourite game at the end. Year 6 loved seeing everyone enjoy their hard work and explaining how their games worked.
It was wonderful to see so much excitement about maths, as well as the fantastic creativity, effort and teamwork shown by our Year 6 pupils. Well done to everyone involved!

About
School Life

Curriculum
At Caterham, we are committed to providing an educational experience that is dynamic, innovative, and tailored to meet the needs of our pupils today. Our curriculum is not a static entity; it’s an ever-evolving framework designed to keep pace with the changing demands of the world.
The integration of technology is a cornerstone of our teaching philosophy, ensuring that it is not just a tool but an integral part of the learning process. Lessons are meticulously crafted to incorporate technological advancements, making the educational journey both exciting and relevant for the pupils. Whether it’s utilising mobile technology, interactive simulations, or collaborative online platforms, technology is thoughtfully embedded to enhance the overall learning experience.
Our commitment to providing a diverse range of learning environments is reflected in the incorporation of a large outdoor classroom. Here, surrounded by 200 acres of woodland, pupils explore and discover, fostering a connection between the theoretical and the practical. Our Global curriculum enriches their educational journey by linking subjects in a meaningful way, promoting a global perspective, and encouraging students to think beyond traditional boundaries.
From the initial play-based learning in Reception to the more formal structures in subsequent year groups, the curriculum evolves to match the developmental progression of each child. The progression is meticulously tracked through a combination of informal and formal assessments, ensuring that each pupil’s unique strengths and areas for improvement are identified and addressed.
Parents play an integral role in this journey, with regular updates on their child’s progress provided through parents’ evenings, open classrooms, and written reports. This collaborative approach ensures a shared commitment to the pupil’s academic and personal growth.
In the Pre-Prep, our youngest pupils embark on their educational journey in Mottrams, a dedicated building that sets the stage for a positive and nurturing learning experience. As they explore, discover, and play, these young learners lay the foundation for a lifelong love of learning that will accompany them through their educational journey at Caterham.

Digital EDGE
With innovation at the heart of what we do, Caterham Prep has achieved national and international recognition for its innovation with both technology and curriculum design.
“Why not?” is a question we ask ourselves a lot, especially when it comes to looking for ways to do things better. Digital EDGE is about equipping every pupil to become an independent, creative and collaborative problem-solver in the digital age. By exploring robotics, coding, 3D design, media, R&D, product design and applied AI, we aim to cultivate a strong foundation in digital skills and innovation that can be applied throughout the curriculum and beyond the school gates. Through hands-on experiences, pupils learn to apply their knowledge and skills to real-world challenges, nurturing an entrepreneurial mindset and equipping them with the tools necessary to excel in any field in a world in which collaboration, communication, problem-solving and confidence with technology are not nice-to-haves but key skills.
Digital EDGE starts in Reception and continues through the prep school, senior school to Sixth Form. Lessons might see children coding and customising robots and drones to conduct rescue missions in disaster zones, creating interactive programmes to help other children learn about ancient cultures or online safety, working alongside an AI co-worker and in flexible development teams to create bespoke mobile apps or creating and producing their own 3D designs.
Beyond lessons, Innovation Pioneers Club runs multiple times per week, giving children the opportunity to work on projects and new skills outside the curriculum, teach and learn from one another, work with companies to test and refine new products and even launch business ventures of their own. All of these skills become part of the ‘toolkit’ that children can bring with them to apply throughout their education and into the world beyond school with confidence and safety.

EDGE
EDGE stands for Explore, Develop, Grow, Evolve and is our unique curriculum that prepares children for the future by equipping them with essential competencies such as problem-solving, oracy, philosophy and collaboration. By teaching study skills and offering language courses like Mandarin, we aim to foster adaptability, resilience, and critical thinking. Through engaging, relevant, and forward-thinking experiences, we empower children to become lifelong learners, poised for success in the fast-changing world in which they will grow up.

Global
Global is the key to a really modern curriculum and is unique to Caterham. Instead of teaching the traditional siloed subjects of history, geography and religious studies, we create globally aware pupils by looking at the past, present and future of carefully chosen topics through our global lessons. The topics begin with a big question ranging from “Where am I?” in Year1, to ” What happens if we don’t have clean water? in Year 5, through exploration of these discussions, the children gain an appreciation of other cultures, belief systems and physical and human geographical reasons for choices made, thus equipping the children to be able to make informed and meaningful decisions about future events they will inevitably face.
